name: ThreeSum1960614_Machine_Bundle012
definition_title: Executable residue, subset-address, and quartic-switch interfaces
natural_language_statement:
The library defines concrete light-language routines for Cartesian positional-key rows, Pascal-table binomial lookup, exact original-value bucket testing, positive-query filtering, padded residue histograms, integer scale initialization, shifted residue keys, and compact subset ranks. A subset rank is evaluated recursively in the remaining width using stored powers of two and Pascal coefficients. The finite bucket representation retains original physical indices and their multiplicities. Valid stored reporting prefixes have exactly the prescribed length and row cardinality; their signed subset query is explicitly zero when validity or the fixed original-index key check fails.

For natural parameters $J,j,r,q$, the quartic switch tests the exact integer comparison
$$100000000(159243801J+500000000j)r^4\le500000000(J-j)q\bigl(785174904r^3+q(72447023r^2+q(24044466r+12022459q))\bigr).$$
Its candidate set restricts $q$ to $0\le q\le\lfloor r/2\rfloor$, and its index is the least accepted candidate when one exists, with default zero otherwise. The source includes the stated adaptation of the pinned Apache-2.0 switch construction. The library also specifies the wrapper from the 3SUM task's array layout to the benchmark end statement, and reindexes block subset queries into row-major machine coordinates.

These definitions expose the actual programs and finite data behind the reporting and parameter-selection stages of the deterministic integer 3SUM proof. Their placement records specify helper procedure locations; later theorems establish execution, resource bounds, and agreement with the semantic counts.

name: ThreeSum1960614_Machine_Bundle013
definition_title: Concrete cover selection, residue buckets, and positional-key programs
natural_language_statement:
This library defines light-language programs for balancing offsets, band lookup, block coefficients, local cover selection, local cover rows, bit-mask erasure, modulo counts, recursive mask hash evaluation, prime-pool construction, positional-key products, retained bucket-pair testing, selected-index gathering, and physical residue-bucket construction. Procedure-number parameters identify the helper bodies to be called; the accompanying invariants relate current loop counters, local frames, written array prefixes, and preserved memory to the corresponding finite mathematical objects.

For a positive scale $y$, the prime-pool program tests the integers in $(y,4y]$ and appends the accepted primes in increasing order. For a residue-key map $k$ on $N$ original positions and $M$ buckets, prefix offsets and cursor scatter construct contiguous fibers. Each original position is written once, including positions carrying equal values. Bucket selection reads adjacent offsets and returns their difference when its independent endpoint flag is true, and zero otherwise. The retained-pair tester counts exact equalities $a+b=c$ over the selected physical fibers; an empty right fiber bypasses the left scan. Positional-key products retain every record sequence and repeated key.

These executable interfaces implement the cover, key, and bucket operations required by the deterministic integer 3SUM reporting argument. They make iteration counts and memory preservation explicit rather than assuming constant-time access to a semantically specified enumeration.
